We're going to be doing a discussion for each episode of the Zelda Unknown Series by Commonwealth Realm. As character discussions will be posted on mondays, these discussions will happen every tuesday friday until we've finished the series. Since we move a little slowly, the discussion will be featured all day every Tuesday, but you're free to keep replying until we start the next discussion next week! So please don't feel discouraged from replying if the discussion has been up for a while.

In the absence of Zelda Wii U info from Nintendo, what we're left with is speculation, and the Zelda Unknown series by Commonwealth Realm is an excellent source of that. So let's get started with episode 1: The return of Snowpeak!

Please watch the episode and then join us: Zelda Unknown - The return of Snowpeak.

For reference, here is the Zelda U world map: https://veuwer.com/i/2uae.png

To start us out I will post a summary of the episode in my own words for reference and then pick a few topics for discussion, but don't feel obligated to stick only to those.

Episode Summary

The Snowpeak region of Hyrule is the area that has appeared the least frequently in all of the games. It only appeared as Snowpeak in Twilight Princess, though there were also similar winter-themed regions that appeared in Majora's Mask (Snowhead) and Four Swords Adventures. Based on the map that has been revealed for the world of Zelda U, it is very likely that we will be getting another winter region similar to Snowpeak this time around.

In Majora's Mask, Snowhead was, oddly enough, the home of the gorons. It included several major activities, including: Obtaining the Lens of Truth, helping the deceased goron, obtaining the goron mask, and learning the Goron's Lulluby. It was divided into several sections: Snowhead, the Mountain village, the lake leading up to the Goron village, the Goron village, and the dungeon itself.

The second major Winter region was Snowpeak itself as it appeared in Twilight Princess. This region was a vast area where the two main points were the house of the Yetis, unique characters to the Twilight Princess world, and the dungeon.

After a recap of the past Winter areas, we get into speculation on what Zelda U's might be. He divides this speculation into five different sections:

Geography: Zelda U developer Aiji Aonuma has stated that one region in Zelda U will be comparable in size to the entire overworld in Twilight Princess. As it is fairly certain the top northwestern region of the new map is a Winter region, we will be getting an absolutely massive Winter area in the upcoming game. He provides a side-by-side comparison of the two maps. Activities based on the geography may include climbing vast mountain ranges, skiing, hunting. The Winter region would be an excellent area to showcase next-gen weather effects, particularly the Aurora Borealis.

Towns and Villages: There should be a mountain town or village with many sidequests and dynamic NPCs where you participate in the winter culture (possibly even with its own variant of the Hylian language) and acquire items necessary for traversing the Winter landscape.

Races: So far the races that have appeared in Winter areas are Gorons and Yetis. As the gorons will probably be in Death Mountain in Zelda U, he speculates that the Yeti race will return to the Snowpeak region. He suggests that there could be two variants to the Yeti species, one that is friendly (similar to the Zoras in most games, and as the Yetis were in Twilight Princess) and one that view link as an enemy and are hostile (like the Zora variant in Link to the Past and other games).

Wildlife: As we saw at the gameplay footage of Zelda U, wildlife is being implemented much more heavily in this game than previous entries. The forest/field region showed horses, goats, and deer, and he speculates that each region will have its own particular wildlife that serves different purposes. The Winter region could have Mountain Goats, Reindeer, Eagles, Snow Leapords, Wolves and Bears as an example.

Dungeon: The dungeon in Zelda U should be well-hidden in the vast winter region, with a subquest itself focused on finding it. The dungeon should be unconventional and compelling, and utilize puzzles like the Snowpeak dungeon did in Twilight Princess.

The Snowpeak region is perfect for including in-game surprises and unconventional sidequests.

Topics for Discussion

These are the topics I have chosen for discussion on this episode. Feel free to reply only to certain ones if you don't have an opinion on all of them! I also encourage you let us know about any topics that were of interest to you that I might not have down here, and may add them to the list as well.

  1. So far, the Winter region has only appeared in games in the child Link timeline. What do you think the connection between this could be? Does this imply that Zelda U might also take place in the child timeline?

  2. What are your experiences with the past Winter regions of Hyrule and Termina? Which is your favorite? Do you hope the region in Zelda U is more similar to Snowpeak (TP) or Snowhead (MM)?

  3. What do you think of Conrad's (the Commonwealth Realm creator) map comparison between Snowpeak and the northwestern region of Zelda U? Is this compelling evidence that the region is influence by Snowpeak and possible a future iteration of it?

  4. Conrad mentions several activities that could be introduced based on the geography of the region (skiing and mountain climbing, for example). What are some activities you hope are added?

  5. What do you think the town(s) present in this region will be like? What races do you think will occupy them? What activities or sidequests might take place here?

  6. Do you think wildlife will be as big a part of Zelda U as Conrad speculates, or are there maybe just a couple different animals throughout the world that are more decoration than a game element? If you do agree that each region will have its own specific wildlife, what do you think the wildlife of this region will be like?

  7. What did you think of the past Winter dungeons in the series, and what are your hopes for the new one in Zelda U?

Well, this didn't get any replies! If anyone still wants to comment feel free, it's still open for discussion =) Next week's thread is now up as well!
